reason: The law has applied in full since August 2021, and the Commission reports the Agency executing its enhanced tasks and powers, which is independent evidence of application. The Agency also reports supervisions finding violations, and its own strategy says too many controllers fail to apply measures, so application is real but incomplete. One audit dates the law 2018, which is a date discrepancy and not a status conflict.
The law was adopted in February 2020 but controllers had a transition period to August 2021, so before then it was adopted and not yet fully applied. This earlier row marks the change that matters.

Parliament adopted the law on 27 June 2025 and it applies by its own terms from 1 June 2026, but no item shows measures carried out after that date. By-laws had a 15-month deadline, and the Commission found the Reform Agenda step not achieved and asks for further amendment. The 2026 Agency list calling it a proposal is only a list of opinions given, so it is not a real conflict.

The Commission reports in November 2025 that the country adopted a long-term ICT strategy and action plan, and the strategy text says some activities began before formal adoption. The goals in the text are targets, so they do not show delivery. The link between the Commission's sentence and SMART/MK is inferred from timing and is for the analyst to confirm.

The plan remains valid, and measures have been carried out in part: the Commission records 5G expanding to Skopje and biannual Broadband Competence Office reports. Commission reports for 2021 and 2022 record delay, and the Office's own report finds most 5G goals met but none of the three measures on 100 Mbps subscriptions implemented. These sources describe different parts of the plan, so they do not conflict.

The law was adopted in 2019 and some rulebooks and the interoperability platform are in place, but the State Audit Office found only 2.93% of obliged institutions connected and parent laws not aligned. I rely on the audit over the government's description of the framework, so this is not in_practice. The 2025 strategy still calls for full application.

The Commission says the system was introduced in 2013 and has reduced waiting times, the World Bank describes it in use for appointments, and a mobile application and new modules have been added. Both also report limits: referrals still on paper in 2024, and no interoperability with Health Insurance Fund data as of 2025. Those limits qualify the use but do not contradict it.

The roadmap was adopted in December 2022 and the Commission records the first phased reduction in charges starting in October 2023. The Commission is reporting on its own regional process, and the end goal for 2027 remains ahead.

North Macedonia reports the function fully operational from 1 April 2019, and the Commission's own assessment in the 2023 screening report says the system provides for efficient and transparent appeals. This is the latest evidence, and nothing later contradicts it.
The Assembly adopted the law on 22 April 2025, and it enters into force eight days after publication. Its provisions only rename ministries and bodies, and no item shows any further step.

The items in the input are plans, but later Commission evidence shows the Law on Security of Networks and Information Systems adopted in June 2025 and the cybersecurity strategy adopted in January 2025, and the step accepted as achieved although alignment is not complete. The 15 by-laws and the operational authority fall under later steps, and no item shows them delivered. The law itself is a separate entity.

The Agency adopted the rulebook on 26 December 2024 and says it began to apply on 1 July 2025. Entry into application is not evidence that controllers or the Agency carried it out, and the only source is the Agency's own report, so I have not used the stated implemented.

The Commission reports that the first European Digital Innovation Hub in the country was set up, and it refers to making use of the hubs in April 2026. Further support to companies is still recommended, and no item shows the hub's use.

The Commission states in its own words, in 2023 and 2025, that company registration and filing can be carried out fully online in a solid and available one-stop shop. It also describes the digitalised registration as efficient, and no source disagrees.

The catalogue was added to the e-services portal, but the State Audit Office found outdated user lists, only one training session and unpublished services, giving inaccurate and incomplete information. I rely on the audit, so this is not in_practice. The audit reports poor data and does not say that the system does not function, so unclear does not apply.

The law was adopted in 2019, and the audit and government sources describe an operating register that is used as a basis for electronic identification. The evidence of use is descriptive and mostly from government, and the 2025 strategy says the data set must be expanded, so I stop short of in_practice.

The amendments were adopted in April 2021, and the Commission notes that the Personal Data Protection Agency was not consulted beforehand. No item shows biometric identification being used at an election.

The Commission reported in 2021 that use of the red flags contributed to enhanced administrative control by the Bureau, and in 2023 that the portal includes the system. It still asks for further development, and there is no evidence after 2023.

The Commission and the State Audit Office both say AI is being piloted in the 112 service for transcription and translation, so a pilot is in place, but no item shows routine use. The entity includes the EENA pilot, which the sources do not explicitly equate with this one, and that is for the analyst to confirm.

The law gave the Ministry of Digital Transformation its competences, and that allocation is in place. Audit and strategy evidence shows gaps in carrying them out: no accountability line with the Fund for Innovation and Technology Development, and no central register of systems. I therefore do not rate it in_practice.
The agreement was signed on 30 June 2023 and the country joined the programme. No item shows actual participation in calls, and in January 2025 the Commission was still urging active participation.

The Council was established in September 2022, and the 2025 strategy describes it as formed to plan and coordinate digitalisation. The State Audit Office could not confirm any activities in 2023 and reports an absence of activities and results, so a named body exists but is said not to function. I give the audit more weight than the government's description, and there is no later evidence of activity.
The Reform Agenda says the customs administration still has to establish this system, and no item shows it built or in development.

The platform was a Reform Agenda step due by June 2026, and the enabling archival law was adopted in June 2025. No item shows the platform established, and the October 2025 strategy says the infrastructure is missing.
